apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential
curl -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --profile minimal
. "$HOME/.cargo/env"
cd starship
cargo test --locked -- folder_with_maven_config_does_not_trigger_module
issue_paraphrase: Rendering the prompt inside a directory that merely contains an .mvn folder (for example a user-level Maven config directory holding only .mvn/maven.config, with no pom.xml or wrapper properties anywhere) wrongly activates the Maven module, so an empty version tag with the Maven symbol appears in the prompt. The Maven segment should only show for real Maven projects, i.e. when a pom.xml or Maven wrapper properties file is found.
fix_summary: Removed '.mvn' from the maven module's default detect_folders and made detection also require/match maven-wrapper properties files, so an .mvn directory alone no longer triggers the maven module.
notes: AUTHORING HAZARD: starship keeps unit tests INLINE in the source file, so there is no separate test file to `git show <fix>:<path>` from. Do NOT paste the whole fixed file over the parent tree (it contains the fix). For maven #7426 the golden test is only the single function `folder_with_maven_config_does_not_trigger_module` (void, io::Result-based) that the fix commit adds inside `mod tests` in src/modules/maven.rs; copy just that function (with the two lines above it: '#[test] fn ... -> io::Result<()> {') into the parent's `mod tests` block after `folder_without_maven_files`; it compiles unchanged on the parent tree (uses only tempfile::tempdir, fs::create_dir_all, File::create, ModuleRenderer::new("maven").path(...).collect()). Snapshot: parent commit d0e24680. The buggy line to confirm at parent: src/configs/maven.rs default detect_folders = vec![".mvn"]. Build: cold build ~10-11 min on 64 cores (deps + 2.8GB target/), 60-90 min at 1 CPU; incremental bin rebuild ~2-15 min; the target unit test runs in <1s. No pty/shell/network needed for this test. Avoid other module integration tests that shell out to git/svn. Verified 2026-09-11 on bench-base:ubuntu-24.04 (rustc 1.98.1), both directions.

install_recipe:
apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential
curl -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --profile minimal
. "$HOME/.cargo/env"
cd starship
cargo test --locked -- test_empty_textgroup
issue_paraphrase: In prompt format strings, an empty textgroup whose only purpose is to set a color, such as [](bg:#9A348E), is discarded entirely, so it cannot establish the style that later segments should inherit through prev_fg/prev_bg references. Concretely, [](bg:red)[X](bg:prev_bg) renders the X with no background at all, because the preceding empty group produced no segment for prev_bg to refer back to.
fix_summary: When a textgroup's format is empty, the formatter now still emits one empty segment that carries the textgroup's style, so prev_fg/prev_bg references resolve against it and the rest of the prompt inherits the intended foreground/background.
notes: AUTHORING HAZARD: starship keeps unit tests INLINE in the source file; do NOT paste the whole fixed src/formatter/string_formatter.rs over the parent tree (it contains the fix). The golden tests are the three functions test_empty_textgroup_with_style, test_empty_textgroup_without_style and test_empty_textgroup_propagates_prev_bg that the fix commit adds inside the existing `mod tests` block; copy just those three functions (with their '#[test]' attribute lines) into the parent's mod tests, e.g. right before the pre-existing test_nested_conditional; they compile unchanged on the parent tree (they use only StringFormatter::new, .parse(None, None), Segment value()/style()/ansi_string(None)/style_ref() and nu_ansi_term::Color::Rgb, all present at parent). Snapshot: parent commit 0dd5a4f402. Buggy code to confirm at parent: the textgroup parse path in parse_textgroup calls parse_format(textgroup.format, ...) directly so an empty format yields zero segments. Build: cold ~10-11 min at 64 cores, 60-90 min at 1 CPU; incremental bin rebuild ~2-15 min; tests <1s. No pty/shell needed. The CLI check: format "[](bg:red)[X](bg:prev_bg)" renders plain 'X' (1 byte) at parent vs '\x1b[41mX\x1b[0m' at fix. Verified 2026-09-11 on bench-base:ubuntu-24.04.

Note: the starship explain column misalignment itself needs pre-colored module output (e.g. colored custom-command output) and is hard to reproduce headless inside a pty at default widths; the maintainers' own regression test (the grapheme-width unit test) is the authoritative check and it fails at parent / passes at fix as recorded.

install_recipe:
apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential
curl -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --profile minimal
. "$HOME/.cargo/env"
cd starship
cargo test --locked -- test_grapheme_aware_width
issue_paraphrase: The width function used to lay out the 'starship explain' breakdown table measures a module's value by its raw byte length, so ANSI color escape sequences embedded in the value are counted as if they were printable characters. Whenever a module's output contains color codes (for example pre-colored text emitted by a custom command), explain pads the columns with the wrong number of spaces and the module value and description columns end up misaligned.
fix_summary: Pre-compiling a regex for ANSI CSI color sequences ('\x1B\[[0-9;]*m') and stripping those codes inside width_graphemes() before measuring grapheme widths, so non-printing escape sequences no longer inflate the measured width.
notes: AUTHORING HAZARD: the golden test is an INLINE unit test in src/print.rs, and it is a MODIFICATION of a pre-existing test function: the fix commit changes test_grapheme_aware_width (which exists at the parent too) by adding the single line assert_eq!(11, "\x1B[35;6mnormal text".width_graphemes()); after the existing 'normal text' assertion. Do NOT paste the whole fixed src/print.rs (it contains the fix); patch the parent's test function with that added assertion only. With the assertion added, the test compiles and FAILS at parent (left: 11, right: 17) and PASSES at fix. Snapshot: parent commit 109a6811. Buggy code to confirm at parent: width_graphemes() in src/print.rs measures the raw string (no ANSI stripping). Build: cold ~10-11 min at 64 cores, 60-90 min at 1 CPU; incremental bin rebuild ~2-15 min; test <1s. No pty/shell needed. The user-visible symptom (explain column misalignment) requires pre-colored module output and a terminal; it is hard to reproduce headless, the width unit test is the authoritative check (the maintainers' own regression test). Verified 2026-09-11 on bench-base:ubuntu-24.04.
